summary: [standards] The name tests use the code under test as their oracle in places: gate_git_env_02 loops over ALLOWED_ENV and asks env_to_remove, so the membership of 9 of the 11 allowed names is pinned only by ALLOWED_ENV.len()==11 (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_SSH_COMMAND are named, the other nine could be swapped for others unseen; the CHANGELOG test names 5 of the 11); the GIT_TRACE=1 and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/PARAMETERS rows of 01 cannot fail even with no removal (-U3 and -c beat them, as the brief measured), so only GIT_DIFF_OPTS proves that command() applies env_to_remove to the real environment (mutation: env removal emptied -> 01 fails on GIT_DIFF_OPTS); 'canon's own variables keep their values' is shown by get_envs() of a process that holds none of them, not by a shell that holds GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1 (probe with a wrapper git: the child sees GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and only the 11 names + canon's own); gate.git-boundary.01 (canon-store) no longer asserts that command() removes anything (the loop over CLEARED_ENV became env_to_remove(REMOVED_BY_0_39).len()==13), the binary test keeps that. Blast radius: every git child of the process: ls-files, cat-file --batch, add -A on the scratch index, write-tree, migrate's rm/mv/add -f, log/show of the policy history; all are run by the real-binary probe, none has a test of its own for the allowed names.
